content_sections.body: Use this lesson language to communicate a simple real-life meaning: Use I am and My name is to introduce yourself. Model: “My name is Minh. I am a student.” Notice the important words and the word order. Mẹo tiếng Việt: hãy hiểu ý của cả câu trước, rồi nói theo cụm ngắn; không cần dịch từng từ.
content_sections.title: Form and meaning

content_sections.body: Read this short situation. A learner needs to use names and introductions clearly and politely. One useful response is: “My name is Minh. I am a student.” Say the model once, then change one safe detail such as a name, place, time, colour, or item when the meaning allows.
content_sections.title: Guided context

content_sections.body: Practise for meaning, not only for memory. Imagine one everyday situation where names and introductions is useful. First use the model, then make one small change. Check: Is the message clear? Is the target language in the right place? Can another person answer you?
content_sections.title: Use it

exercises.prompt: Complete the natural sentence about names and introductions: My name is Minh. I am _____.
Put these two parts in a natural order to make a message about names and introductions.
Make a short, personal response about names and introductions. Use the lesson language and add one detail that is yours.

criteria: The response communicates a clear meaning about names and introductions.
The response uses the allocated language in an understandable form.
The response adds an appropriate personal or invented detail.

language_focus: Use I am and My name is to introduce yourself.
objectives: Use I am and My name is to introduce yourself.
Use introducing yourself in one short, clear everyday exchange.

constraints: Do not reveal the transcript before the learner answers.
Ask exactly one comprehension question before showing the transcript.
Use only the supplied project-authored transcript.
listening.goal: Understand one clear detail in a short exchange about names and introductions.
listening.instruction: Listen once without reading to a short exchange about names and introductions. Answer the question, then ask to see the transcript and listen again.
listening.question: What is Minh's class?
listening.transcript: Hello. My name is Minh, and I am in class 6A.

constraints: Assess pronunciation only when learner audio is available.
Return NOT_ASSESSED when no audio is supplied.
Give one observable sound, stress, or rhythm point rather than general pronunciation advice.
pronunciation.goal: Produce the identified sound, stress, or rhythm feature clearly in a useful phrase.
pronunciation.instruction: Read the concrete sound target aloud: Link My name is; do not pause between name and is. Then read one lesson sentence slowly and once at normal speed.
pronunciation.target: Link My name is; do not pause between name and is.

constraints: Give the tutor one role and the learner one role before the first turn.
Create an information gap: the tutor asks for one missing personal or practical detail.
Use no more than three tutor turns and give one correction only if it blocks meaning.
Finish after the learner has used the target and responded to one follow-up.
speaking.goal: Complete a short, understandable exchange about names and introductions.
speaking.instruction: Roleplay: you are a learner using names and introductions; the tutor is a helpful conversation partner. Scenario: you need to use this language in a short everyday interaction. Tutor opening: “Hello. Can we practise names and introductions?” Reply naturally, ask or answer one follow-up question, and finish the exchange politely. Useful model: My name is Minh. I am a student.

constraints: Wait for the learner draft before feedback.
Give at most two brief improvement points about meaning, word order, or target use.
Do not replace the learner draft with a complete rewritten answer.
writing.goal: Produce a short A1 message about names and introductions with a clear meaning.
writing.instruction: Write 2–3 short sentences for a real-life situation about names and introductions. Include one sentence pattern from this lesson, then add one true or invented detail. Do not copy this model exactly: My name is Minh. I am a student. Submit your draft first.

title: Names and introductions
